per_question.question: In its fiscal 2020 10-K, how does Expand Energy (Chesapeake) describe its approach to managing commodity price risk with derivatives, including how it values them and handles counterparty non-performance risk?
per_question.answer_markdown: Chesapeake uses oil, natural gas and NGL derivatives to reduce exposure to price swings and to stabilize cash flows [1]. It settles all of these instruments net and did not designate any open derivatives for hedge accounting as of December 31, 2020 [2]. It values them using established index prices, volatility curves and discount factors, and compares these estimates with counterparty valuations for reasonableness [3]. Non-performance risk is considered in that valuation, but has not had a material impact to date [4]. For counterparty risk, it enters into derivative contracts only with highly rated or acceptable-credit counterparties and attempts to limit exposure to any single counterparty [5]. Counterparty obligations must be secured by cash or letters of credit when mark-to-market amounts owed to Chesapeake exceed defined thresholds [6]. The filing also warns that a counterparty default could hurt Chesapeake's ability to fund its planned activities [7].
